t: You're looking at a terrace of listed buildings, numbers 75 to 82, with their original railings still in front, in the Camden streets near Russell Square. William Durrant Cooper died in one of these houses in 1875. He was a lawyer by profession, but he is remembered as an antiquary, someone who spent his spare hours studying and recording the past. It's a quiet reminder that these ordinary-looking London terraces have sheltered a lot of scholarly lives.
